The complete current text was obtained on this pass and closes the review's open question. The conditional discharge sits at Miss. Code Ann. § 41-29-150(d)(1) and the expungement remedy at § 41-29-150(d)(2); the last enacted amendment is Laws 2010 ch. 460 § 2 and there has been none since. Eligible offences are violations of § 41-29-139(c), simple possession, and § 41-29-139(d), paraphernalia; sale, distribution and manufacture under § 41-29-139(a) are outside the route, and the relief is unavailable where the court accepted the plea and adjudicated guilt. The prior-record restriction, the once-only limitation, the Bureau of Narcotics nonpublic record, the application procedure and the mandatory hearing are as summarised in the controlling authority. The section specifies no fee and § 99-19-72's fee does not reach it.

Trafficking-survivor relief under Miss. Code Ann. § 97-3-54.6, as amended by 2026 HB 1546 effective 1 July 2026, is recorded here as a separately-listed matter and NOT as a tenth normalized source node, because neither the adopted Batch 2 memorandum nor the authoritative source crosswalk lists it among Mississippi's nine core adult slots. The enrolled text was read: new § 97-3-54.6(6) lets the sentencing court, at any time after a conviction or adjudication of delinquency of a misdemeanour or a felony not classified as a crime of violence under § 97-3-2, expunge on appropriate motion where it finds by a preponderance that participation in the offence occurred during the period the person was being trafficked and was the direct result of that trafficking; official documentation from a federal, state or local government agency creates a presumption but is not required; and new § 97-3-54.6(7)(b) provides that neither failing to raise the trafficking affirmative defence nor the court's finding on it affects the ability to file under subsection (6). This relief is broader and faster than ordinary § 99-19-71 conviction expungement, so screening for it belongs on every intake. Whether it becomes a normalized node requires an express crosswalk or memorandum instruction.

Whether the Miss. Code Ann. § 99-19-72 fee reaches a given petition. The section reads: 'A filing fee of One Hundred Fifty Dollars ($150.00) is hereby levied on each petition to expunge an offense under Section 99-19-71 to be collected by the circuit clerk', distributed $100 to the Judicial System Operation Fund, $40 to the District Attorneys Operation Fund and $10 retained by the circuit clerk. Last amended by Laws, 1st Ex. Sess. 2017, ch. 7, § 12; no enacted amendment through 2026. Two things remain unresolved on its face and are NOT resolved by construction here. First, the trigger is 'each petition to expunge AN OFFENSE under Section 99-19-71': a § 99-19-71(4) non-conviction petition is a petition under § 99-19-71 but is not a petition to expunge an offence, because there is no conviction, and the statute does not settle it either way. Second, the collection mechanism names the CIRCUIT CLERK, which does not map onto § 99-19-71(1) or (4) petitions filed in justice or municipal court. Sections 9-11-15(3), 21-23-7(6), 99-15-26, 63-11-30, 41-29-150 and 67-3-70 sit outside § 99-19-71 and the fee does not reach them by its terms; none of those sections specifies a fee of its own. The packet therefore publishes NO fee amount on any track and instructs the participant to confirm the filing fee, and any pauper's-affidavit route, with the clerk of the court before filing.

The complete current text was obtained on this pass and resolves the review's open questions on this track. The expungement provision is Miss. Code Ann. § 63-11-30(13), from enrolled SB 2095 (Laws 2022 ch. 303), which is the last enacted amendment — no 2023 to 2026 amendment touched it, and 2026 HB 1546 changed only § 99-19-71(2). The waiting period is confirmed as at least FIVE years after successful completion of all terms and conditions of the sentence, and it was NOT affected by HB 1546's reduction of the general felony period to three years. Venue is confirmed as the circuit court of the county in which the conviction was had. One practical caution survives: the provision is widely cited as § 63-11-30(14), and per the enrolled act (13) is Expunction while (14) is Nonadjudication, so the subsection letter should be confirmed against the current print before filing.

The complete current text of Miss. Code Ann. § 67-3-70 was obtained on this pass from enrolled HB 917 § 34 (Laws 2020 ch. 314), the last enacted amendment, with no enacted amendment 2021 to 2026. This CLOSES the review's open question: the one-year waiting period is now supported by primary authority rather than by a secondary clearinghouse source, the covered offences are subsections (1) and (2), the trigger is the later of dismissal and discharge or completion of any sentence and payment of any fine, venue is simply 'the court', and relief is mandatory on the findings. What the section does not supply is petition contents, prosecutor notice, hearing procedure or a fee, none of which it prescribes; the packet therefore drafts to the statutory findings and instructs the participant to confirm any filing fee with the clerk.
